LESSON: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING- COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we tell the meaning of words and phrases in a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main ideas in a text
2. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text
3. describe characters, ideas, or events in a text
4. appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING- COMPREHENSION
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING- COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the main ideas in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the main ideas in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the main ideas in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the main ideas in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe characters, ideas, or events in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to describe characters, ideas, or events in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe characters, ideas, or events in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe characters, ideas, or events in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the main ideas in a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension to a partner. (skill: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: describe characters, ideas, or events in a text)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the main ideas in a text.
3. Practise this skill: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text.
4. Practise this skill: describe characters, ideas, or events in a text.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we tell the meaning of words and phrases in a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the main ideas in a text.
5. Be able to: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
